- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the first 10–15 days of the forecast horizon.
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., 70.93 → 72.65), then overcorrects with high later values.
- Tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, particularly in the middle of the forecast window.
- Mean reversion bias: forecasts often settle near historical mean (67–69) too early, missing sustained upward trends.
- Overestimates volatility in early forecast days, especially when history shows low-to-mid range prices.
- Underestimates late-period spikes (e.g., 70.93 → 72.65) and fails to capture momentum in the final 5–7 days.
- Forecasts show persistent downward bias in the last 5–7 days of the 30-day window, even when true prices are rising.
- Model reacts too slowly to recent high prices; fails to anticipate continuation of upward trends.
- Overconfident in early forecast days, leading to underestimation of true price peaks.
- Tends to overcorrect downward movements, creating artificial rebounds that don’t materialize.
